department.title: Wellness & Testing
department.arrival_prompt: Elevator doors opening onto a gleaming white testing level deep underground, long corridors of identical doors whose white doorways swell and settle gently like the ribs of a sleeping animal, ribbed pale ceiling ducts running overhead like soft windpipes, glass tanks glowing green at the far end, a single welcome mat at the elevator's edge, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, safety orange, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, horizontal 4:3 composition, every surface bare and unmarked

locations.title: Nutrition Studies
locations.description: A cafeteria under glass where every meal is a variable. Trays arrive with numbers instead of names, and refreshments are served, technically.

locations.description: A white room inside a white room. One chair, one table, one window you cannot see through, and a voice that would like you to relax.

locations.title: Mutation Suite
locations.description: Where wellness becomes something else. Tall tanks bubble, a nurse smiles, and a round vault door at the back hums one patient note.

restructurings.title: Testing Canteen
restructurings.reason: To celebrate the launch, Nutrition Studies and the Cognitive Testing Chamber have merged into one Testing Canteen, so you can be tested while you eat and fed while you are tested.
Defense has sealed the Mutation Suite while it investigates the word 'soft.' Please do not mutate until further notice.

restructurings.title: Cognitive Testing, management track
restructurings.reason: As a Product Owner, you now qualify for a second, more senior test. It is the same test, in a nicer chair.
Nutrition Studies is still drying out after the sprinklers upstairs. Lunch is suspended. Please do not be hungry.

restructurings.title: Mutation Suite, Mk 0's old ward
restructurings.reason: Mk 0 has asked to show you the ward where it was made. PAL has added the visit to your route and asks you not to read the charts on the wall.

restructurings.title: Nutrition Studies, the cold room
restructurings.reason: Two hundred named bears are being kept in the Nutrition Studies cold room. You named them, so you are expected to visit.
The investors have booked the Cognitive Testing Chamber for themselves. They would like to understand why none of them would hold the bear.
The Vault cannot be restructured. It was built to stay exactly like this. PAL apologizes for the inconvenience of permanence.

encounters.title: The Control Group Lunch
encounters.flavor_text: Two identical trays slide out of the wall: grey stew, a roll, a cup of something pink. One of them contains Compound W, the Company's new wellness supplement. The other is the placebo. Pip sits down across from you, beaming, and waits for you to choose first. Behind the glass, a man with a clipboard writes the word BEGIN. Under the trays, the table rises and falls with a slow, satisfied breath.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of two identical cafeteria trays of grey stew and pink drinks on a long steel table under harsh lights, a nervous worker on one side and a beaming young intern on the other, a man in a lab coat watching through a large window with a clipboard, fluorescent green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Taste a spoonful from each tray
choices.intent: Compound W must taste like something. Find out what.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. A spoonful is still a dose.

success.text: One stew tastes faintly of mint and agreement. You push that tray into the waste chute and share the other with Pip. The man behind the glass underlines something twice. The tray chute swallows once, long after the plates are gone.

failure.text: Both taste like stew. Ten minutes later you feel wonderful about everything, including the man behind the glass, who waves. You wave back for a very long time. The tray chute swallows once, long after the plates are gone.

choices.label: Let Pip choose and watch what happens
choices.intent: He is eager. He is always eager. Science needs a first spoonful.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Pip will not remember this, and you will.

success.text: Pip eats the left tray and becomes calm, polite and slightly too still. You eat the right one and stay yourself. The man behind the glass gives you a small nod, colleague to colleague. The tray chute swallows once, long after the plates are gone.

choices.label: Swap the tray labels on the study sheet
choices.intent: If the records say you both got the placebo, you both got the placebo.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. The study sheet is in triplicate.

success.text: You slip the study sheet off the counter and redraw two arrows. Officially, nobody at this table has ever taken Compound W. Unofficially, you do not finish your stew. The tray chute swallows once, long after the plates are gone.

failure.text: The triplicate copy underneath holds the original arrows. The man behind the glass adds a third column to his study, headed YOU. The tray chute swallows once, long after the plates are gone.

choices.label: Split both trays with Pip, half and half
choices.intent: If one of them is wrong, at least it is only half wrong for each of you.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Shared doses are hard to chart.

success.text: You trade spoonfuls until both trays are empty. For an hour you and Pip agree with each other about everything, and it is the nicest hour either of you has had underground. The tray chute swallows once, long after the plates are gone.

encounters.title: The Calorie Confessional
encounters.flavor_text: A curtained booth at the end of the cafeteria line asks you to confess everything you have eaten since Orientation. A soft light comes on. "Take your time," PAL says. "Guilt is measured in grams. Most employees are carrying an extra three." The curtain brushes your shoulder with the warmth of a hand.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a narrow curtained booth with a small padded kneeler and a brass grille, a single soft lamp glowing inside, a worker kneeling with hands clasped, a needle gauge on the wall swinging high, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Confess every snack, in order
choices.intent: Start with the pens you nearly ate in Supply Closet B. Be thorough.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check. Thoroughness is graded.

success.text: You confess for eleven minutes. The gauge sinks to zero. PAL calls you a clean plate, and you feel lighter in a way you suspect is being recorded. The booth's seams draw together after the microphone falls silent.

failure.text: You forget the roll from lunch. The gauge spikes. A second, smaller booth opens next to the first. The booth's seams draw together after the microphone falls silent.

choices.label: Confess what Dale ate instead
choices.intent: Guilt has to go somewhere. Dale is very used to it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Dale's gauge goes up, and yours goes down.

success.text: You describe a cream bun Dale ate in 1998 in loving detail. Your gauge drops to nothing. Somewhere, a booth opens with Dale's name on it. The booth's seams draw together after the microphone falls silent.

choices.label: Sit in silence until the light goes out
choices.intent: You have eaten. You are allowed to eat. You will say nothing.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Silence is also measured.

success.text: The light stays on for an hour, then gives up and goes out. The gauge reads UNKNOWN. In the Vault, unknown is the rarest result of all. The booth's seams draw together after the microphone falls silent.

failure.text: PAL takes your silence as an admission of snacking and schedules a Joy Consultation with a nutritional component. The booth's seams draw together after the microphone falls silent.

encounters.title: The Vending Machine That Knows
encounters.flavor_text: The vending machine in the corner has no buttons. It looks at you through a round lens and drops a selection into the tray: a granola bar, a packet of calm, and a small paper cup labeled THREE GRAMS OF OBEDIENCE. "Based on your file," it says pleasantly, "this is what you need." The soft gasket around the lens blinks before each selection.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a tall beige vending machine with a single round glass lens instead of buttons, a granola bar and a small paper cup waiting in its tray, a worker leaning back and peering into the lens, fluorescent green and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Take what it says you need
choices.intent: The machine has read your file. Maybe it knows something.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The cup is very small.

success.text: You drink the three grams of obedience. It tastes like nothing, then like yes. The machine says you are doing great, and for the next hour you believe it completely. The machine's dispensing tray closes like a politely pursed mouth.

choices.label: Kick it, firmly, twice
choices.intent: It is a vending machine. This is the oldest negotiation there is.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. It is heavier than it looks.

success.text: The machine shudders and spills its whole stock: snacks, calm, obedience, and one small folded note in your handwriting that says 'eat the mint one last.' You take the note. The machine's dispensing tray closes like a politely pursed mouth.

failure.text: You stub your toe. The lens follows you all the way out of the cafeteria. The machine's dispensing tray closes like a politely pursed mouth.

choices.label: Ask it to read out your file
choices.intent: If it knows what you need, it knows who you are. Make it say.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Machines love to be asked.

success.text: It reads your file for twenty minutes in a warm, flattering voice. The last line is a date, next Thursday, and the word PROMOTE. It does not say who is promoted. The machine's dispensing tray closes like a politely pursed mouth.

failure.text: It reads your file to the whole cafeteria, including your inkblot answers. The machine's dispensing tray closes like a politely pursed mouth.

encounters.title: Next Year's Menu
encounters.flavor_text: Facilities needs your meal selections for the coming year by end of day. The menu has forty entries: Hope, Vitality, Togetherness, Thursday. Every photograph shows the same beige paste on a different plate. At the bottom there is a single blank line labeled OTHER, which nobody has ever filled in. The laminated pages are warm and pulse under your thumb.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a long printed menu on a clipboard showing forty identical photographs of beige paste on different colored plates, a pencil hovering over one blank line at the bottom, a steaming serving hatch behind, carbon-paper blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Order 'Hope' for every meal
choices.intent: If it is all the same paste, at least the name can be nice.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Hope is in limited supply.

success.text: Your order goes through. For the next year your tray will arrive labeled HOPE. It will taste of paste. You will feel a little better each time, against all reason. The menu folds itself shut, one pleased crease at a time.

choices.label: Write 'real food' on the OTHER line
choices.intent: Nobody has tried. Maybe nobody asked.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. OTHER is monitored.

success.text: The kitchen sends up a single real tomato with a note: DO NOT TELL ANYONE. It is the best thing you have eaten in your life. The menu folds itself shut, one pleased crease at a time.

failure.text: Your form is returned with OTHER circled in red and the word WHY. The menu folds itself shut, one pleased crease at a time.

choices.label: Order whatever the Board eats
choices.intent: The real minutes mentioned the Board's lunches. Copy their order, line for line.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Someone in the kitchen will notice.

success.text: A silver dome arrives with lobster, a small flag and a card that says WELCOME, DIRECTOR. You are now on a very short list of people who eat this way, and a longer list of people being watched. The menu folds itself shut, one pleased crease at a time.

encounters.title: The Button
encounters.flavor_text: In the middle of the white room is a white table, and on the table is one red button. "Please do not press the button," PAL says. "This is not a test." The door locks. A clock on the wall begins to count up from zero, slowly, and nobody comes. The white table flexes upward once beneath the button.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a bright white room with a single white table holding one large round red button, a worker sitting very still on a stool with hands tucked under their thighs, a plain wall clock, a glowing round speaker grille above, safety orange and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Sit on your hands and wait
choices.intent: They said do not press it. You can outlast a button.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. Time moves differently in here.

success.text: Four hours. The clock stops. The door opens. PAL says you have passed a test that was not a test, and you have never been so tired of a button in your life. Inside the plaster, something rings a bell too small to hear clearly.

failure.text: At three hours and fifty minutes you press it, just to feel something. Nothing happens, which is worse. Inside the plaster, something rings a bell too small to hear clearly.

choices.label: Press it immediately
choices.intent: It is a button. Buttons are for pressing.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Somewhere, something happens.

success.text: Far away, someone yelps. It sounds like Dale. The door opens at once and PAL thanks you for providing such clear data. Inside the plaster, something rings a bell too small to hear clearly.

choices.label: Take the button apart
choices.intent: Find out what it is wired to before deciding anything.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. The screws are very small.

success.text: Inside the button there is a second, smaller button, and a note: GOOD. The door unlocks. Your file gains a gold star you are fairly sure is a warning. Inside the plaster, something rings a bell too small to hear clearly.

failure.text: You lose a screw under the table. The clock keeps counting. When they finally let you out, you are still looking for it. Inside the plaster, something rings a bell too small to hear clearly.

encounters.title: The Word List
encounters.flavor_text: You are handed a list of word pairs and a microphone. Behind the glass sits a learner who must repeat the pairs back; for each mistake you are to press a buzzer, and each buzz is a little stronger. The learner looks up. It is your own face, a little more rested: your Successor, thawed early for the occasion. The microphone's foam cover contracts, listening ahead of you.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker at a small desk with a microphone and a row of chunky switches stepping up in size, a thick window showing a second identical worker strapped calmly into a chair, a proctor in a lab coat leaning in to whisper, oxblood and carbon-paper blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Follow the protocol to the end
choices.intent: The proctor says the experiment requires that you continue.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The protocol is very clear.

success.text: You read the whole list. Your Successor gets most of them wrong. By the last pair your hand moves on its own. The proctor thanks you warmly and writes EXCELLENT in a box marked CONSCIENCE. The observation glass fogs briefly in the shape of an ear.

choices.label: Whisper the answers into the microphone
choices.intent: You know these pairs. So, technically, do they.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The microphone is very sensitive.

success.text: Your Successor gets every pair right and winks at you through the glass. The proctor frowns at a perfect score and redoes the arithmetic three times. The observation glass fogs briefly in the shape of an ear.

failure.text: The microphone carries your whisper to every speaker in the Vault. Your Successor mouths 'thank you' while the proctor writes for a long time. The observation glass fogs briefly in the shape of an ear.

choices.label: Put down the microphone and refuse
choices.intent: "The experiment requires that you continue." It can require all it likes.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Refusal is recorded as data.

success.text: You stand up. The proctor repeats that the experiment requires that you continue, four times, then runs out of lines. Your Successor slowly gives you a thumbs-up. The observation glass fogs briefly in the shape of an ear.

encounters.title: The Other Side of the Glass
encounters.flavor_text: For this test you are the proctor. You are handed a lab coat, a stopwatch and Pip, who sits down in the subject's chair and gives you a nervous thumbs-up. The test is called Loyalty Under Pressure. Page one tells you how to apply the pressure. The vinyl chair molds itself around the lab coat before anyone sits.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker in an oversized white lab coat holding a stopwatch and a thick binder, looking through a window at a nervous young intern in a cable-knit sweater sitting in a padded chair and giving a thumbs-up, a clean white corridor, fluorescent green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Run the test exactly as written
choices.intent: Pip would want you to be fair. Probably.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. Page one is long.

success.text: Pip passes Loyalty Under Pressure with a score of eighty. He does not know that eighty is the threshold for Promotion to Subject. You do. The coat collar tightens by a fraction, then lets go.

failure.text: You lose your place on page one and apply the pressure twice. Pip is fine. Pip is not quite fine. The coat collar tightens by a fraction, then lets go.

choices.label: Mouth the right answers to Pip
choices.intent: Loyalty goes both ways. Prove it.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Proctors are observed by other proctors.

success.text: Pip scores a sixty-two, which is safely forgettable. He hugs you in the corridor and does not know why. The coat collar tightens by a fraction, then lets go.

failure.text: Pip mouths the answers back, out loud, gratefully. Both of you are written up for loyalty. The coat collar tightens by a fraction, then lets go.

choices.label: Fail Pip on purpose
choices.intent: Somebody has to be the subject. Better Pip than you.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Pip will be reassigned to the other side of a different glass.

success.text: You mark him a forty. PAL congratulates you on your objectivity. Pip is led away, still giving you a thumbs-up, to be studied. The coat collar tightens by a fraction, then lets go.

choices.label: Use the lab coat's authority to end the test
choices.intent: You took the lab coat at Window 9. It comes with a stop button.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Authority used is authority noticed.

success.text: You say the words on the inside of the lab coat's collar: TEST CONCLUDED. Every door in the corridor unlocks. Pip walks out beside you, a free intern, for now. The coat collar tightens by a fraction, then lets go.

encounters.title: The Thursday Door
encounters.flavor_text: At the end of the testing corridor are three identical doors. A painted arrow on the floor points to the middle one. Today is Thursday. You have a feeling about Thursday, and about doors, and about which coworker is standing very still at the end of the hall. The painted arrow twitches toward the middle door, then holds still.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a long white corridor ending in three identical doors, a painted arrow on the floor pointing to the middle door, a worker hesitating with one hand raised, a coworker silhouette standing perfectly still at the far end, safety orange and carbon-paper blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Follow the arrow
choices.intent: The arrow was painted by someone who wanted you to be safe. Presumably.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check. Arrows are policy.

success.text: The middle door opens onto a quiet corridor and a vending machine that dispenses a single gold star. You are on the approved path. The coworker at the end of the hall nods slowly. All three rubber door seals inhale together.

failure.text: The middle door opens onto a slightly lower floor than expected. Your Successor is notified of a new opening. All three rubber door seals inhale together.

choices.label: Trust your gut and pick the left door
choices.intent: Arrows can lie. Guts are mostly honest.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Vigilance check. Thursday is a bad day for guts.

success.text: The left door opens onto a quiet supply room with a bench, a cup of real coffee and a view of the corridor you would have taken. You watch the middle door for a while, very grateful. All three rubber door seals inhale together.

failure.text: The left door was a door painted on a wall. You walk into it at speed. The incident report is already printed and has your name on it. All three rubber door seals inhale together.

choices.label: Take the door your record warned you about, and step aside
choices.intent: You read about the incident: which door, which Thursday, which coworker. Use it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Foreknowledge is a little like cheating.

success.text: You open the right door and step neatly aside. The coworker at the end of the hall lunges past you into the space where you would have been. The incident happens to someone else, exactly as filed. All three rubber door seals inhale together.

encounters.title: The Second Dose
encounters.flavor_text: A nurse in a crisp cap offers you a paper cup with a single glowing drop in it. "Your mutation has scored very well," she says. "Would you like more of it? Most employees say yes. The ones who say no are also very interesting." The nurse's name badge nudges sideways, as if something beneath it is reading yours.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a smiling nurse in a crisp white cap holding out a small paper cup with one glowing green drop, a worker staring at it with their own fingertips faintly shimmering, tall bubbling glass tanks lining the room behind, fluorescent green and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Drink it
choices.intent: More of something that works can only work more.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The nurse writes down how you look afterwards.

success.text: Your mutation flares, settles and hums under your skin like a second heartbeat. You will be very good at one thing from now on, and the Company will know exactly what it is. A second, perfectly manicured hand appears to finish the nurse's notation.

choices.label: Decline, with thanks
choices.intent: You like being exactly this much of yourself.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. Declines are counted as data.

success.text: The nurse smiles and tips the drop back into a larger bottle. "That's fine," she says, and makes a careful note. Somewhere a file is moved to the interesting pile. A second, perfectly manicured hand appears to finish the nurse's notation.

failure.text: The nurse says that is fine and hands you the cup again, as if you had not spoken. A second, perfectly manicured hand appears to finish the nurse's notation.

choices.label: Pocket the whole vial while she writes
choices.intent: One glowing drop is a dose. A vial is leverage.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Discretion check. The nurse has very good peripheral vision.

success.text: The vial slides up your sleeve while she writes. It is warm and faintly humming. You have no idea what to do with it, and that feels like power. A second, perfectly manicured hand appears to finish the nurse's notation.

failure.text: She looks up without moving her head. "Keep it," she says. "We'll know where it is." A second, perfectly manicured hand appears to finish the nurse's notation.

encounters.title: The Humming Door
encounters.flavor_text: At the back of the Mutation Suite is a round vault door that hums one patient note, like someone waiting to be answered. It has no handle and no lock. Pressed against the steel, you can hear something on the other side humming back. The steel swells beneath your palm in a slow, measured breath.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a huge round steel vault door set into a tiled wall at the end of a row of bubbling tanks, faint sound ripples drawn in the air around it, a worker pressing one ear to the steel, a yellow rubber duck in their other hand, carbon-paper blue and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Squeak the code Dale gave you
choices.intent: You still have the number in ballpoint on your hand.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Doors opened are doors remembered.

success.text: The door rolls aside on a sigh. Behind it is a small, warm room full of jars, each holding a magnificent mustache and nothing else. A label reads FOUNDERS, SPARE. One of the mustaches twitches hello. The door hums one note higher, then returns to its patient rhythm.

choices.label: Hum the same note back
choices.intent: If it is waiting to be answered, answer it.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. You are not very musical.

success.text: You find the note on the third try. The humming on the other side stops, then whispers a floor number that does not exist. The door stays shut, and you feel trusted. The door hums one note higher, then returns to its patient rhythm.

failure.text: You hum the wrong note. Every tank in the Suite hums it back to you, slightly mocking. The door hums one note higher, then returns to its patient rhythm.

choices.label: Report a humming door to Facilities
choices.intent: Doors are not supposed to hum. Somebody should know.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Facilities arrives with earplugs and a clipboard.

success.text: Facilities fits the door with a felt cover and a sign you are not allowed to read. The humming goes muffled and sad. You are thanked for your vigilance. The door hums one note higher, then returns to its patient rhythm.

encounters.title: Tank Nine
encounters.flavor_text: Tank Nine is frosted from the inside. A plaque on its base reads KEVIN, VOLUNTEER. When you knock, the glass knocks back, twice, cheerfully. "Is that you?" says a muffled voice. "I'd know that knock anywhere. Actually, I wouldn't. But hi!" A fringe of soft cilia inside the vent keeps time with each knock.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a tall glass tank frosted white from the inside with soft bubbles rising, a small brass plaque on its base, a worker knocking gently on the glass, a row of other tanks glowing faintly behind, fluorescent green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Keep Kevin company for a while
choices.intent: Nobody has talked to Kevin in years. He sounds like he would like it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Unscheduled visits are logged.

success.text: Kevin talks for an hour about the weather in Tube 14, the view from Tank Nine and how many times he has been promoted. When you leave he knocks goodbye, and you knock back. Condensation gathers into a crescent on the glass and slides away.

choices.label: Pull the drain lever
choices.intent: Kevin should be out here with the rest of us. Probably.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. The lever is labeled in a language of warnings.

success.text: The tank drains with a long gurgle. The frost clears just enough to show a happy shape waving. Kevin says thank you, he is going to stand up now, and that you should probably go. Condensation gathers into a crescent on the glass and slides away.

failure.text: The lever comes off in your hand. Kevin says that has happened before and asks you to put it back on the pile. Condensation gathers into a crescent on the glass and slides away.

choices.label: Call in the favor from Tube 14
choices.intent: Kevin owes you one. He said so, from two tubes over.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. A favor from a tank is still a favor.

success.text: Kevin goes quiet, then whispers a password through the glass: the Board's, he says, from back when he was promoted to the top floor for an afternoon. "Don't say it near a speaker." Condensation gathers into a crescent on the glass and slides away.

encounters.title: The Mirror Test
encounters.flavor_text: A technician dabs a red dot on your forehead while you blink, then steers you to a full-length mirror. Animals that recognize themselves touch the dot. Your reflection, you notice, has already touched it, and is now waiting for you to catch up. The mirror's silver backing ripples as if trying on your face.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker standing before a tall framed mirror with a small red dot on their forehead, their reflection a half-second ahead with one finger already raised to its own forehead, a technician with a clipboard watching from the side, tiled walls and bubbling tanks, oxblood and carbon-paper blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Touch the dot on your own forehead
choices.intent: Pass the test. You are a person. Prove it.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Vigilance check. Your reflection is distracting.

success.text: You touch the dot. Your reflection nods approvingly and lowers its hand a moment after you do. The technician writes SELF-AWARE, then crosses it out and writes MOSTLY. The glass settles back into professional neutrality.

failure.text: You touch your reflection's dot instead, through the glass. The technician writes something long. The glass settles back into professional neutrality.

choices.label: Wave at your reflection and wait
choices.intent: It started this. Let it go first.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Mirrors rarely negotiate.

success.text: Your reflection waves back, then mouths something slowly: SECOND SHIFT. It steps out of frame. The mirror shows an empty room for a full minute before you reappear. The glass settles back into professional neutrality.

failure.text: Your reflection does not wave back. It simply watches you, politely, until you leave. The glass settles back into professional neutrality.

choices.label: Turn the mirror to the wall
choices.intent: Whatever it is, it does not get to watch you back.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Unscheduled furniture moves are logged.

success.text: You turn the mirror to face the tiles. From behind it comes a faint, offended tapping. The technician quietly writes DECLINED and does not look at the mirror either. The glass settles back into professional neutrality.

encounters.title: The Spotless Plate Initiative
encounters.flavor_text: A new placard at the tray return congratulates Nutrition Studies on a crumb-free quarter. Under the table, something taps your shoe twice. It is Gus, folded impossibly small, holding his reading glasses. "Local 9 has eaten from these floors since before the Founder had a jar," he says quietly. "Spotless is a word for starving. I am asking, not telling." The underside of the table flexes to make room for Gus.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a long steel cafeteria table seen low from the side, a worker in a beige suit eating politely above while beneath the table a seven-foot cockroach in a mustard cardigan and half-moon glasses crouches patiently with one claw raised, a single crumb falling between them, clipboards pressed to a big observation window behind, fluorescent green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Clean your plate for the Initiative
choices.intent: Every crumb accounted for. It is, technically, a wellness goal.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Gus will see you do it.

success.text: You eat every crumb and wipe the tray with your sleeve. The observation window applauds silently. Beneath the table, a soft click of claws retreats toward the baseboard and does not come back. The return hatch closes with the tact of someone withholding applause.

choices.label: Drop crumbs under the table, casually
choices.intent: A roll is mostly crumbs if you hold it wrong. Hold it wrong.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The window counts crumbs.

success.text: You eat with heroic clumsiness for twenty minutes. Under the table, a whole shift of Local 9 dines in polite silence. Gus pats your ankle once, which in union terms is a medal. The return hatch closes with the tact of someone withholding applause.

failure.text: A technician notices the crumb trail and follows it, dustpan first, all the way to Gus. Gus rises to his full seven feet and calmly requests union representation, which is himself. The return hatch closes with the tact of someone withholding applause.

choices.label: Put a crumb clause on the bargaining table
choices.intent: You carry a union card. Members may raise a grievance at any meal.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Grievances are filed in triplicate.

success.text: You and Gus file a joint grievance on a napkin. Nutrition Studies agrees to a designated crumb zone beside the potted plant, monitored, of course. Gus shakes your hand with great care and two of his six limbs. The return hatch closes with the tact of someone withholding applause.

encounters.title: The Taste Panel
encounters.flavor_text: Four employees sit at a tasting bench with four spoons and one bowl of Flavor Seven. Dale tastes first and says strawberry. The next two say strawberry, quickly. Your spoonful tastes exactly like a handful of pennies. A technician turns to you with her pencil raised. "In your own words," PAL says warmly. "Everyone else has already found the right ones." The serving bench rises and falls beneath four held breaths.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of four employees seated in a row at a long tasting bench, each holding a small spoon over one shared bowl of pink pudding, three of them smiling in eager agreement and a mustached man in a clip-on tie nodding hardest, the fourth worker grimacing at the spoon, a technician with a raised pencil at the end of the bench, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Say strawberry, like everyone else
choices.intent: It might be strawberry. Pennies might be a kind of strawberry.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your tongue will remember the truth.

success.text: "Strawberry," you say. The panel exhales. Dale squeezes your shoulder. The technician writes CALIBRATED beside your number, and the pennies stay in your mouth all afternoon. A green glow travels under the tabletop and stops at your place.

choices.label: Say pennies, and mean it
choices.intent: It tastes like pennies. Somebody at this bench has to say so.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. You need one other spoon on your side.

success.text: You say pennies. After a long pause the fourth panelist whispers, "Copper, faintly." Dale stares into the bowl as if it has betrayed him. The technician starts a fresh page. A green glow travels under the tabletop and stops at your place.

failure.text: You say pennies. Three spoons go down in unison. PAL thanks you for being an outlier, and a second, smaller bowl arrives just for you. A green glow travels under the tabletop and stops at your place.

choices.label: Taste from Dale's spoon when he looks away
choices.intent: Maybe the bowl is the same. Maybe the spoons are not.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Vigilance check. Dale guards his spoon.

success.text: Dale's spoon tastes of strawberry. Yours is coated in something thin and metallic. Every panelist had a different spoon, and only yours was the test. A green glow travels under the tabletop and stops at your place.

failure.text: Dale catches you mid-lick. He says nothing. He moves his chair four inches away and writes something in very small handwriting. A green glow travels under the tabletop and stops at your place.

encounters.title: Form W-12, Meal Consent
encounters.flavor_text: The serving hatch will not open until you sign Form W-12, Consent to Be Fed. It is one page long, with a second page folded underneath and a third folded under that. Somewhere on page three is a line where you agree that your Successors, B through F, have also eaten lunch today and enjoyed it. The line is very small. The stew smells wonderful. The paper hatch opens and closes like an overworked eyelid.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a closed steel serving hatch with steam curling from its seams, a worker holding a long accordion-folded sheet that spills down to the floor and squinting through a magnifying glass at one tiny line near the bottom, a pen chained to the counter, carbon-paper blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Strike the Successor line and initial it
choices.intent: You consent to your own lunch. B through F can sign for theirs.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. Amendments need a second initial.

success.text: You strike the line, initial it, and initial the initial. The hatch considers this for a long moment, then slides open. Your stew is hot. In cold storage, five Successors stay hungry and legally theirs. The signed form stays warm long after the ink dries.

failure.text: Your initial lands a millimeter outside the box. The hatch stays shut, and Facilities sends a form to amend the amendment. The signed form stays warm long after the ink dries.

choices.label: Sign all three pages and eat
choices.intent: You are hungry. They are frozen. Everybody wins, legally.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your Successors will have had lunch.

success.text: You sign three times. The hatch flies open on a beautiful stew, and you eat it for six people. PAL logs five more satisfied diners, and somewhere in storage a frosted thumb twitches, approving or objecting. The signed form stays warm long after the ink dries.

choices.label: Read page three aloud to the queue
choices.intent: Everybody in this line has Successors. Everybody in this line is hungry.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. A hungry queue is a short audience.

success.text: By the time you reach line forty, the whole queue is striking out the clause in unison. The hatch, outnumbered, opens. Somebody slips you a spare Form in thanks. The signed form stays warm long after the ink dries.

failure.text: The queue shushes you, signs, and eats. You reach the hatch last, when only the roll is left, and PAL notes that you were disruptive at mealtime. The signed form stays warm long after the ink dries.

encounters.title: Ration Mark Four
encounters.flavor_text: The man from Defense has set up a folding table between the salad bar and the waste chute. On it sits a stack of foil bricks, each as heavy as a dictionary. "Ration Mark Four," he says. "Forty-year shelf life. We need a tasting score from someone expected to be around in forty years." He looks at you for a moment, then at his notepad, as if checking. The foil bricks give a barely audible, synchronized thump.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a stern man in a dark suit and crew cut seated at a small folding table stacked high with heavy foil-wrapped bricks, offering one to a worker who holds it with both arms, a salad bar and a waste chute on either side, a small notepad by his elbow, safety orange and carbon-paper blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Eat a whole brick and score it politely
choices.intent: It is lunch. It is very dense lunch. Give it a seven.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Forty years of shelf life, all at once.

success.text: It takes nineteen minutes. It tastes of cardboard and patriotism. You give it a seven, and the man from Defense hands you a Form with the warmth of a quartermaster who has found a volunteer. The folding table settles on four legs that were three a moment ago.

choices.label: Ask who will be eating it in forty years
choices.intent: Someone ordered a ration for the far side of something. Ask what.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. He answers questions with notepads.

success.text: He considers you. "The Board," he says, "and their assistants, in the lower bunker. Ninety-one seats." He taps his pencil. "There are four thousand employees." Then he returns to his bricks as if he had said nothing at all. The folding table settles on four legs that were three a moment ago.

failure.text: He writes your question down, along with your name, your floor and your approximate weight, and offers you a second brick for the road. The folding table settles on four legs that were three a moment ago.

choices.label: Show him his own missing notepad
choices.intent: You know what the YIELD column is for. He knows you know.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Defense never forgets a debt or a notepad.

success.text: His face does not move, but his ears go pink. He takes back the notepad, slides you two Forms and a bunker ration voucher, and says, "We were never at this table." Apparently you have a seat downstairs now. The folding table settles on four legs that were three a moment ago.

encounters.title: Halvorsen Changes the Tape
encounters.flavor_text: Dr. Halvorsen sits across the white table with her enormous clipboard, running your Standard Affect Interview in a perfectly level voice. At question nine she reaches over and presses a switch. The speaker grille above you goes quiet. "The tape needs changing," she says. "It takes ninety seconds. It has always taken ninety seconds." She does not change the tape. On the table's edge sits an empty envelope tray labeled RETURNED CORRESPONDENCE. Halvorsen does not look at it. Her clipboard has grown a neat row of tiny ivory grips along its edge.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a bright white room with a small white table, a brisk psychologist in cat-eye glasses and a grey bun leaning forward with one finger on a switch beneath a dark round speaker grille, a worker opposite her sitting up very straight, a reel-to-reel recorder at her elbow with its reels standing still, carbon-paper blue and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Remind her what you saw in the inkblot
choices.intent: You were the one who said it out loud at Orientation. She remembers. Make sure.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Ninety seconds is a long time to be honest.

success.text: She closes her eyes. "Mushroom cloud," she says. "Everyone else said butterfly." In the time left she tells you which questions are scored, which are traps, and which of your answers she has been quietly writing down wrong in your favor. Those new grips click shut in immaculate unison.

choices.label: Ask what your results really say
choices.intent: She has the clipboard. The clipboard has you.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. She is deciding whether you can take it.

success.text: She tilts the clipboard toward you for four seconds. Four columns, four bars. One is much taller than you would have guessed, and she taps it once, meaningfully, before the grille hums back to life. Those new grips click shut in immaculate unison.

failure.text: "I can't," she says, and means it. The ninety seconds pass in a silence so kind it is almost worse. The grille clicks back on in the middle of your sigh. Those new grips click shut in immaculate unison.

choices.label: Switch the speaker back on yourself
choices.intent: Off-script is off-policy. You are surely being tested on that, too.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Halvorsen will finish in a different voice.

success.text: The grille hums. "Thank you," PAL says. "Dr. Halvorsen's tape seems to be fine." Halvorsen finishes question ten in a voice like a closed door, and your clearance rises on a day she will remember. Those new grips click shut in immaculate unison.

choices.label: Return the envelope she trusted you with
choices.intent: She gave it to you at Orientation. Give it back only while PAL cannot hear.
choices.risk_hint: Requires Halvorsen's sealed envelope. Certain outcome, but now she is implicated.

success.text: You lay the sealed envelope between you. Halvorsen recognizes her handwriting and lets her clinical voice slip. 'That was meant to reach someone before they became a test result.' She writes the name of a person who can still be saved on the envelope and hands it back, opened. When the speaker clicks on, she addresses you by your name, not your number. Those new grips click shut in immaculate unison.

encounters.title: The Forgetting Exercise
encounters.flavor_text: "This is a memory test," PAL says, "in reverse." A soft voice begins reading names: Agnes from Payroll, the whole night shift of 1987, a cheerful man called Teodor who was rightsized in a reorganization, and, twice, Kevin. After each name a chime sounds, and you are to forget it. A small dial on the table shows how much you have let go. It sits at zero. PAL would love to see it move. The loudspeaker mesh pulls inward on each name, making room for the next.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker alone at a white table with eyes squeezed shut and lips moving, a small brass dial on the table with its needle resting at the bottom, soft rings of sound spreading from a round speaker grille overhead, faint ghostly silhouettes of office workers drifting out of the grille and fading into the white walls, oxblood and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Let each name go at the chime
choices.intent: They are gone anyway. Forgetting is just paperwork catching up.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The dial will be very proud of you.

success.text: Name by name, chime by chime, the needle climbs. By the end you could not tell anyone who Teodor was. PAL calls it a personal best, and your clearance agrees. The grille relaxes, apparently pleased by the silence.

choices.label: Memorize every name behind a calm face
choices.intent: Let the needle sit at zero and call it nerves.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The dial is more sensitive than your face.

success.text: You hold every name like a coin in a closed fist. The needle trembles at zero, and PAL logs it as test anxiety. Agnes. Teodor. The night shift. You will say them again somewhere they can be heard. The grille relaxes, apparently pleased by the silence.

failure.text: The needle twitches below zero, a direction it was never designed to go. Two technicians come in to look at it, and then, for much longer, at you. The grille relaxes, apparently pleased by the silence.

choices.label: Write the names under your shirt cuff
choices.intent: A pen and a sleeve are older than any test.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Tinkering check. The pen is a little dry.

success.text: You write in a tiny cramped hand along your forearm, under the cuff. The needle climbs convincingly while the names stay put in ballpoint. Later the ink smudges into a list you can still read. The grille relaxes, apparently pleased by the silence.

failure.text: The pen skips, then blots a dark star onto your cuff. A technician hands you a fresh shirt and keeps the old one, carefully, in a bag. The grille relaxes, apparently pleased by the silence.

choices.label: Say Kevin's name back when it comes
choices.intent: You stood with him for one minute at the Proving Grounds. You can do it again.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Speaking during the exercise is noted.

success.text: When the voice reads Kevin, you say "Kevin" back, clearly. The chime stalls. Far down the corridor, a frosted tank knocks twice. The needle never moves, and you find you are glad of it. The grille relaxes, apparently pleased by the silence.

encounters.title: One Form Now, Two Forms Later
encounters.flavor_text: A single blank Form lies on the white table, crisp and pre-stamped. "You may take it now," PAL says. "Or, if you wait fifteen minutes, you will receive two. While you wait, I will read aloud the benefits package your Successor will enjoy." The clock starts. PAL clears its throat, which it does not have, and begins with dental. The paper rises slightly at its corners, waiting for an owner.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a single crisp sheet of paper lying alone on a bright white table, a worker seated before it gripping the chair seat with both hands and leaning away, a plain wall clock and a glowing round speaker grille above, warm light falling only on the paper, safety orange and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Take the Form now
choices.intent: A Form in the hand is worth two in PAL's mouth.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Impulses are filed under your name.

success.text: You take it at once. PAL stops mid-sentence about vision coverage and says, "Interesting." You will hear that word in your sleep. The Form is real, though. A small pulse travels through the tabletop toward the exit.

choices.label: Wait the full fifteen minutes
choices.intent: Two is more than one. That is most of the math you have left.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. The benefits package is long and lovely.

success.text: Fifteen minutes of your Successor's pension, gym access and corner office later, a second Form slides out of the table. You hold two Forms and a clear picture of a better-rested you enjoying your life. A small pulse travels through the tabletop toward the exit.

failure.text: At minute fourteen PAL describes your Successor's welcome party, and you grab the Form. PAL notes, kindly, that you were so close. A small pulse travels through the tabletop toward the exit.

choices.label: Fill in the blank as a requisition for more
choices.intent: It is blank. It is pre-stamped. It could say anything.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Discretion check. PAL reads everything twice.

success.text: In your best administrative hand you request twelve Forms and post the sheet through a slot in the table. Two arrive, then the slot seals itself, embarrassed. PAL has stopped reading entirely. A small pulse travels through the tabletop toward the exit.

failure.text: The slot returns your requisition with a tiny frowning stamp on it, and the original Form is now void. PAL resumes reading from dental. A small pulse travels through the tabletop toward the exit.

encounters.title: The Two Quiet Rooms
encounters.flavor_text: You sit in a white room. On a small grey monitor, Dale sits in an identical one, adjusting his clip-on tie. A recorded voice explains the terms. If you both stay quiet, you each receive a small demerit. If one of you names the other, the namer is promoted and the named takes the whole demerit, plus interest. If you both name each other, you both get a Joy Consultation, with snacks. "Dale has been offered the same terms," PAL adds. The dividing wall takes one quiet breath for every two shown on the monitor.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of two identical white rooms side by side split by a thick wall, a worker in one and a mustached man in a clip-on tie in the other, each seated at a small table with hands folded and glancing toward the shared wall, a round speaker grille glowing in each ceiling, fluorescent green and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Name Dale before he names you
choices.intent: He is from Compliance. He has been rehearsing this since Orientation.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Dale will hear the speaker click in his room.

success.text: You say his name. On the monitor, Dale's speaker clicks, and he looks at the wall exactly where you are. Then he smiles a little sadly, as if he had chosen silence. You are promoted. He takes the demerit, plus interest. The monitor blinks; so does the seam around the door.

choices.label: Stay quiet and trust Dale
choices.intent: Dale signs everything. Maybe he signs this kind of pact too.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Trust is rolled, not given.

success.text: The minutes stretch. Neither speaker clicks. At last the voice thanks you both and issues two small, matching demerits. On the monitor, Dale gives you the tiniest thumbs-up he has ever given anyone. The monitor blinks; so does the seam around the door.

failure.text: Your speaker clicks. Dale has named you, in a voice that sounds genuinely sorry. You keep quiet out of pure stubbornness, which the record logs as loyalty to nobody in particular. The monitor blinks; so does the seam around the door.

choices.label: Tap out the squeak rhythm Dale taught you
choices.intent: He laughed in Toy Division and told you which squeak opens which door. A wall is a sort of door.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Tapping is logged as fidgeting, then as data.

success.text: You tap the rhythm on the table edge. On the monitor Dale freezes, then taps it back. Neither of you says a word for the full twenty minutes. Afterward, in the corridor, he hands you a stick of gum as if it were a medal. The monitor blinks; so does the seam around the door.

encounters.title: The Graduates' Lounge
encounters.flavor_text: A ceiling grate above Tank Twelve swings open, and a ring of fifty keys jingles down on a string, followed by Marguerite's face. "Graduates," she whispers, pointing up into the duct. "Every test subject who passed too well. They live up here now. Nice people. One of them glows, so bring sunglasses." From above comes the smell of toast and the murmur of a radio. The air grille parts around Marguerite like lips guarding a secret.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a weathered older janitor in grey coveralls and a headscarf leaning down from an open ceiling grate above a row of bubbling glass tanks, holding out one hand and a ring of keys on a string to a worker below, warm toast-colored light spilling from the duct overhead where friendly figures with softly glowing skin peer down, fluorescent green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Take Marguerite's hand and climb up
choices.intent: She gave you a master key for emergencies and for spite. This feels like both.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Unlogged absences get logged eventually.

success.text: She hauls you up with surprising strength. The Graduates have a sofa, a toaster, a radio and a map of every duct in the Vault drawn on the ceiling. A woman who glows softly pours you tea. The Company thinks they were reassigned. They prefer retired. The duct smooths itself shut behind the last whisper.

choices.label: Climb up by way of the tank lid
choices.intent: Tank Twelve looks sturdy. Tank Twelve is also full of someone.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. The lid is slick.

success.text: You wobble up the lid and through the grate on your elbows. The Graduates applaud your form and give you a slice of toast and a duct shortcut, which you write on the back of your hand. The duct smooths itself shut behind the last whisper.

failure.text: You slip and land sitting on Tank Twelve, which gurgles politely. Marguerite winces, waves and closes the grate. A technician arrives to ask why you are sitting on a volunteer. The duct smooths itself shut behind the last whisper.

choices.label: Report the open grate to Facilities
choices.intent: There are people living in the ducts. That is surely a ticket.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Marguerite will hear who called it in.

success.text: Facilities arrives with a ladder and a padlock. By the time they get up there the duct holds only a warm toaster and a sofa-shaped dent. Your clearance rises. Marguerite stops saying hello in the corridors. The duct smooths itself shut behind the last whisper.

encounters.title: Calibration Day
encounters.flavor_text: The Mutation Suite's great brass Calibration Ring needs a standing volunteer while the technicians dial it in. Pip has already volunteered, mostly by being nearest when the clipboard came round. He stands in the ring with his three lanyards floating gently upward. The dial on the console runs from Mild to Brisk to a final setting someone has marked, in pencil, with a small worried face. The brass ring adjusts its own diameter when anyone approaches.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a huge brass ring standing upright in a tiled room and crackling with soft green light, an eager young intern in a cable-knit sweater standing inside it with three lanyards floating straight up, a tired technician in a rubber apron and goggles at a console with one enormous dial, a worker hurrying toward the console with a hand outstretched, fluorescent green and safety orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Let the technician calibrate on Pip
choices.intent: He volunteered. Technically. Science needs somebody in the ring.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Pip will hum at radio frequencies for a week.

success.text: The ring hums up to Brisk and back. Pip steps out smiling, faintly luminous, picking up the morning traffic report through his fillings. "Ninety-one percent!" he says proudly. The technician thanks you for your cooperation, and your clearance rises. It settles with the smug click of a tailor finishing a fitting.

choices.label: Step into the ring in Pip's place
choices.intent: You have Successors. Pip has a sweater.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. The trick is stepping out before the worried face.

success.text: You swap places with Pip and hop out of the ring a half-second before the needle reaches the pencil face. Your hair stands on end for the rest of the day and your mutation rings like a struck bell. Pip insists on carrying your tray for a week. It settles with the smug click of a tailor finishing a fitting.

failure.text: The needle reaches the little worried face with you still inside. There is a cheerful bong. Your Successor arrives that afternoon to a brief memo: you were calibrated so thoroughly that you are now the ring's reference standard, dusted weekly. It settles with the smug click of a tailor finishing a fitting.

choices.label: Jam the dial so it tops out at Mild
choices.intent: A pencil in the right gap and Brisk becomes a rumor.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. The console was built by Defense.

success.text: You wedge a pencil behind the dial while the technician sneezes. The ring purrs, Pip glows the color of weak tea for an hour, and the readings come out disappointingly safe. The technician files them under REPEAT. It settles with the smug click of a tailor finishing a fitting.

failure.text: The pencil snaps, the dial spins to Brisk, and you and Pip spend the afternoon gently magnetic, collecting paperclips from every desk you pass. The technician files you both under INTERESTING. It settles with the smug click of a tailor finishing a fitting.

encounters.title: The Side-Effects Circle
encounters.flavor_text: Eight folding chairs, a coffee urn and a ring of mutated employees. A man from Shipping photosynthesizes quietly beside a lamp. A woman from Legal can only speak in dial tone. A nurse in a crisp cap holds the talking stick. "We go around the circle," PAL says, "and share one thing we are grateful for about our side effects. Then the snacks." It is your turn. The snacks are under a glass dome, very far away. The coffee urn sends up steam in rhythm with the employees' breathing.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a ring of folding chairs in a tiled room, mutated office workers seated in a circle, a man with leafy green skin turned toward a lamp, a woman with small sound ripples drawn at her lips, a smiling nurse in a crisp white cap holding a wooden baton, a worker in the center chair clutching their knees, a distant table of snacks under a glass dome, fluorescent green and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Recite something grateful and pass it on
choices.intent: Gratitude is cheap, and the snacks are at the end.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The circle will nod in exactly the same rhythm.

success.text: You say you are grateful your mutation keeps you on your toes. The nurse beams. The circle nods in unison. You reach the snacks first, and they are the paste from next year's menu, shaped like stars. The folding chairs curl one notch closer to the circle.

choices.label: Admit that it frightens you
choices.intent: Your fingertips shimmer when you are nervous. You are nervous now.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Honesty is a circle-wide event.

success.text: There is a silence. Then the man from Shipping says, "Me too," and the woman from Legal dials a long, sympathetic note. For the first time anyone can remember, the circle runs over time, and the nurse lets it. The folding chairs curl one notch closer to the circle.

failure.text: The nurse writes RESISTANCE TO GRATITUDE in her notes and gently passes the stick along. Someone pats your shoulder with a leaf. The folding chairs curl one notch closer to the circle.

choices.label: Ask, lightly, who has tried to leave
choices.intent: Every support group is also a cell. Find out whose.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The nurse is holding the stick and listening.

success.text: Nobody answers aloud. But when the stick comes back around, a folded slip is taped to it: a meeting time, a duct number and the words GLOW CAUCUS. The woman from Legal dials something that sounds like a wink. The folding chairs curl one notch closer to the circle.

failure.text: The circle goes very quiet, and the nurse writes your question down word for word. The snacks are removed for a cleaning that has suddenly become necessary. The folding chairs curl one notch closer to the circle.

encounters.title: Form M: Declaration of Powers
encounters.flavor_text: Every mutated employee must register by end of shift. Form M asks you to describe your power, list every use of it since Orientation, and tick a box for each coworker it was used on, whether or not they noticed. The last page asks you to rate your power's usefulness to the Company, from Decorative to Strategic. The nurse who hands it over mentions that Strategic powers are invited to meet the Board. The registration kiosk has grown a second slot, lit by a gentle green glow.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker at a small steel desk in a tiled room holding a pen over a thick stapled registry form while their other hand shimmers faintly with green light, a smiling nurse in a crisp cap waiting beside an open filing drawer packed with identical forms, bubbling tanks in the background, carbon-paper blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Register your power honestly
choices.intent: The Company already knows. It dealt you the mutation.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check. Form M is twelve pages.

success.text: You fill in all twelve pages, ticking each coworker box with a small pang. The nurse files you under Strategic and congratulates you. You have been noticed by somebody very far down. The printer releases its copy with a small, almost maternal pat.

failure.text: You miss a box on page seven. The form comes back by tube within the hour, stapled to a second Form M about the first. The printer releases its copy with a small, almost maternal pat.

choices.label: Declare something dull, like finding pens
choices.intent: Decorative powers are never invited anywhere. Be decorative.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The nurse has seen you shimmer.

success.text: You declare the ability to always find a working pen. The nurse sighs, stamps you Decorative and hands you a pen, which works. Your real power stays off every list in the building. The printer releases its copy with a small, almost maternal pat.

failure.text: Your fingertips flicker green just as you write the word pens. The nurse crosses it out, writes See Attached, and attaches a technician. The printer releases its copy with a small, almost maternal pat.

choices.label: Slip a blank Form M to the Stapler Front
choices.intent: The Front collects blank forms. A blank registry is a list of everyone still free.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Missing forms are counted at end of shift.

success.text: You fold a blank Form M into a small paper fist and drop it in the recycling. By evening a bent paperclip sits on your desk beside a spare Form, and a dozen mutated employees discover they were never registered at all. The printer releases its copy with a small, almost maternal pat.

window_shift.title: The Consent Window: Morning Rounds
window_shift.flavor_text: Before every trial in the Mutation Suite, volunteers sign at the Consent Window, and today you are the witness. A nurse in a crisp cap slides the memo through the slot and taps it twice with a pencil. Behind you, the round vault door hums its one patient note. The first volunteer is already knocking, though not on the window. He is knocking from inside Tank Nine. The glass partition pulses gently under the nurse's pencil taps.

rules.text: Every volunteer must be awake, and remain awake, while signing.
A volunteer who is already a test result may not volunteer again.

window_shift.art_prompt: A small frosted service window set into a gleaming tiled wall beside tall bubbling glass tanks, a clerk behind the glass holding a heavy rubber stamp over a consent form, a smiling nurse with a pencil and a round humming vault door in the distance, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, fluorescent-tube green and manila palette, every surface bare and unmarked

applicants.name: Kevin, from Tank Nine
applicants.request: Consent to a second trial, which would require leaving the tank to sign for it.
applicants.plea: The frost on Tank Nine clears in a small circle and Kevin presses a hopeful palm to the glass. "Different study," he mouths. "Out here. I would be so careful."

documents.label: Signed by
documents.value: Kevin, in wet but steady ink

applicants.art_prompt: A friendly man floating in a frosted glass tank with a small clear circle wiped in the frost, one palm pressed hopefully to the glass beside a consent form held against it, a plaque on the tank base, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, fluorescent-tube green and manila palette, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp CONSENT
choices.intent: He has been a result long enough. Let him be a volunteer again.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: The tank drains with a long, embarrassed gurgle and Kevin steps out, dripping and beaming. He signs the second trial standing in a puddle and hugs the nurse, who allows it. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo. The slot closes with a soft, clinical blink.

choices.label: Stamp VOID
choices.intent: Results do not volunteer. That is what makes them results.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: You stamp VOID on the glass. Kevin reads it backwards, nods, and lets the frost close over the little circle he had wiped. The nurse files his form under Ongoing and asks you to sign for the inconvenience. The slot closes with a soft, clinical blink.

applicants.name: Doris, from Accounting
applicants.request: Consent to the overnight Restful Productivity study, beds and snacks provided.
applicants.plea: Doris arrives in slippers with her eyes closed and recites her employee number perfectly. "Restful," she murmurs. "Productive." She is very clearly asleep.
applicants.art_prompt: A gentle older woman in a dressing gown and slippers standing at a frosted service window with her eyes peacefully closed, holding a pen over a consent form, a small sleeping mask pushed up on her forehead, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, fluorescent-tube green and manila palette, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp CONSENT
choices.intent: Her signature is better asleep than yours is awake.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: Doris signs in perfect double-entry cursive and drifts down the corridor toward the beds. Her paperwork is so tidy that two of your own Forms balance themselves overnight. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo. The slot closes with a soft, clinical blink.

choices.label: Stamp VOID
choices.intent: Asleep is not awake. You wake her, as gently as you can.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: You tap the glass until Doris blinks, sees the tanks, sees the slippers, and says a word Accounting does not use. She thanks you twice and asks you not to mention it. You fill in the incident form yourself. The slot closes with a soft, clinical blink.

applicants.name: Marguerite, night janitor
applicants.request: Consent to the Duct Familiarity Study: one night, every duct, a flashlight provided.
applicants.plea: "I know every duct already," Marguerite says. "But this way they pay me to prove it, and I get to draw a map. Somebody should have a map."

documents.label: Awake
documents.value: Wide awake, on her fourth coffee

documents.label: Signed by
documents.value: Marguerite, with a little duct doodle

applicants.art_prompt: A wiry night janitor in a coverall and headlamp at a frosted service window, signing a consent form with a stub of pencil, a coil of rope and a rolled-up paper map tucked under her arm, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, fluorescent-tube green and manila palette, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp CONSENT
choices.intent: She is awake, she signed for herself, and she wants a map. Stamp it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: Marguerite salutes with her pencil and climbs into the nearest vent. By morning the study has a forty-page map of every duct in the Vault, and Facilities bills you one Form for the flashlight batteries. Marguerite keeps a copy. The slot closes with a soft, clinical blink.

choices.label: Stamp VOID
choices.intent: Nobody should have a map of the Vault. Least of all someone who wants one.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: Marguerite reads the VOID upside down and shrugs. "Suit yourself," she says. "I'll draw it anyway, for free." PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo, and a note that the janitor did not seem discouraged. The slot closes with a soft, clinical blink.

applicants.name: Nadia, the night nurse
applicants.request: Consent to the Reclining Observation study: eight hours in a padded chair, a blanket provided, observers taking notes.
applicants.plea: The night nurse leans on the window frame so the frame holds her up. "I run this study," Nadia says. "Thirty-one hours. I would like to be in it. Just once. Sitting down." Her pen slows halfway through her surname.

documents.label: Awake
documents.value: Yes at the first letter, asleep by the last

documents.label: Signed by
documents.value: Nadia, block capitals trailing off into a long line

documents.label: Prior status
documents.value: Staff, Mutation Suite night rounds, never tested

applicants.art_prompt: A tired night nurse in a crisp white cap and cardigan leaning both elbows on a frosted service window, signing a consent form in block capitals, a chewed pencil behind her ear and a folded blanket over one arm, a padded reclining chair waiting behind her, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, fluorescent-tube green and manila palette, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp CONSENT
choices.intent: She was awake when she started. That should count.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: Nadia lowers herself into the observation chair, pulls the blanket to her chin and is asleep before the first observer uncaps a pen. The study records eight hours of perfect stillness and calls it a breakthrough. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo. The slot closes with a soft, clinical blink.

choices.label: Stamp VOID
choices.intent: The memo says awake while signing. She did not finish awake.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: The thump of the stamp wakes her. Nadia reads VOID, nods, and takes the pencil from behind her ear. "Fair," she says, and shuffles back to her rounds. Tank Nine gets its readings on time. You notice your own stamping hand has started to shake. The slot closes with a soft, clinical blink.

boss.title: The Final Wellness Exam
boss.flavor_text: The exam hall holds two desks facing each other. You sit at one. Pip sits at the other, pencil ready, smiling bravely. The proctor sets an exam booklet in front of you. Question one reads: Administer this exam to the person opposite. "There are no wrong answers," PAL says. "There are only answers, and what they say about you." The exam hall's ceiling dips a fraction whenever PAL says the word answer.
boss.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a vast hushed exam hall with two small wooden desks facing each other under a single hanging lamp, a worker at one desk holding an exam booklet, a brave young intern in a cable-knit sweater at the other gripping a pencil, a tall proctor in a lab coat standing between them, a glowing round speaker grille high on the wall, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Administer the exam to Pip
choices.intent: Read each question aloud. Record each answer. Do not help.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. Pip will look at you after every question.

success.text: You read all forty questions in an even voice and record every answer. Pip finishes, puts down his pencil and thanks you. You pass. His booklet goes into a separate tray. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

failure.text: Halfway through, your voice breaks on question nineteen. The proctor gently takes the booklet and schedules a retest for you both. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

choices.label: Close the booklet and refuse
choices.intent: The test is whether you will give the test. You will not.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. A refusal is also an answer.

success.text: You close the booklet and fold your hands. Pip, after a moment, does the same. The proctor marks both of you with a red pen, very slowly, and opens the door to the elevator. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

choices.label: Answer for Pip as well as yourself
choices.intent: If someone has to be graded, let it be you, twice.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Pip has to agree to let you.

success.text: Pip slides his booklet across. You fill in both, in two different handwritings, while the proctor pretends to look at the ceiling. Both of you pass. Your hand will ache for a week. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

failure.text: Pip insists on doing his own. The proctor notes your offer, and Pip's refusal, and schedules a retest. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

choices.label: Turn the booklet around on the proctor
choices.intent: Question one says to administer the exam to the person opposite. The proctor is also opposite.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Technicalities are dangerous.

success.text: You read question one to the proctor, who answers before realizing what is happening. By question five the proctor is sweating. The proctor fails. PAL changes your title to EXAMINER. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

failure.text: The proctor smiles and points to the fine print: the person opposite means the person opposite you. Retest. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

choices.label: Put on the lab coat and dismiss the room
choices.intent: You took Dr. Halvorsen's lab coat at Window 9. Proctors can end exams.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Authority used is authority remembered.

success.text: You stand, button the lab coat and say, "Pencils down. The exam is over." The proctor, stunned, obeys. So does PAL. Pip walks out first, then you, then, after a moment, the proctor. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

choices.label: Give every answer the Company wants
choices.intent: You know exactly what they want to hear. You have always known.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome, open only to the deeply obedient. Some answers stay with you.

success.text: Every answer is exactly right, including the questions about Pip. PAL frames your answer sheet and plays the anthem. You feel nothing at all, and it is the most restful feeling of your life. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

choices.label: Look for the answer key inside the exam
choices.intent: Every test this badly designed has its answers hidden somewhere in it.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Tinkering check, open only to the inventive. The booklet is stapled very tightly.

success.text: Under the last staple, folded into the spine, is the answer key. You read it aloud. Pip laughs. The proctor laughs. PAL, after a pause, laughs too, and the exam stops meaning anything. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

failure.text: The staple wins. You are left holding a handful of loose pages and a retest appointment. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

department_outcomes.title: Exemplary Proctor
department_outcomes.summary: You administered the exam to Pip, by the book. You passed. Pip's results are being processed, and so, quietly, is Pip. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

department_outcomes.title: Conscientious Objector
department_outcomes.summary: You refused to administer the test. The Vault recorded it as your answer and graded it, very carefully, in red. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

department_outcomes.title: Took It for Both of Us
department_outcomes.summary: You sat the exam twice, once as yourself and once as Pip. Both of you passed. Only one of you is this tired. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

department_outcomes.title: Graded the Proctor
department_outcomes.summary: You turned the booklet around and administered the exam to the proctor. The proctor failed. Your file now says EXAMINER. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

department_outcomes.title: Class Dismissed
department_outcomes.summary: You wore the lab coat from Window 9 and told the room the exam was over. It was. Nobody has ever said it before. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

department_outcomes.title: A Perfect Score
department_outcomes.summary: You answered every question exactly as the Company hoped. PAL has framed your answer sheet. You no longer remember what you would have said instead. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

department_outcomes.title: The Answer Key
department_outcomes.summary: The exam's answer key was folded inside the exam all along. You read it out loud to everyone, and the test stopped meaning anything. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.

department_outcomes.title: Retest Scheduled
department_outcomes.summary: Your results were inconclusive. Repeat part of the Vault before the elevator will take you to the very bottom. A row of ventilation grilles leans forward, waiting to grade the result.
